images.caption: The Riggs–Tompkins Building (also known as The Riggs National Bank, Fourteenth and Park Road Branch) is located at 3300 14th Street NW in the Columbia Heights neighborhood of Washington, D.C. The Classical Revival building was constructed in 1922 and designed by George N. Ray. It currently serves as a PNC Bank branch. In 1985, the building was added to the District of Columbia Inventory of Historic Sites, and in 1987 it was listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

images.caption: Clifton Terrace located at 1308, 1312, and 1350 Clifton Street, NW in the Columbia Heights neighborhood of Washington, D.C. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2001.

Trinity Towers located at 3023 14th Street, NW in the Columbia Heights neighborhood of Washington, D.C. The Gothic Moderne apartment building was constructed in 1928 and designed by local architect Harvey Warwick.
